title: A translation-compatible smooth model of a bounded algebraic group
statement: Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], $E=\operatorname{Frac}(R)$, $k=R/\mathfrak m_R$, and $T=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Fibres and products mean scheme-theoretic base changes [def-pc-base-change]. A group scheme over a base has multiplication, inverse and identity morphisms over that base satisfying the group identities (the diagrams of [def-sc-group-scheme], with the indicated base in place of a field). Separated means that its diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Let $G/E$ be a smooth separated finite-type group scheme [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Choose a geometric point $\bar t$ over the closed point of $T$, put $R^{\mathrm{sh}}=\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{T,\bar t}$ and $E^{\mathrm{sh}}=\operatorname{Frac}(R^{\mathrm{sh}})$ [def-weil-geometric-point, def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]. Suppose $G(E^{\mathrm{sh}})$ is bounded: there is a finite affine open cover $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}B_i$ of $G$, finite $E$-algebra generating lists $(b_{ij})_j$ of $B_i$, sets $C_i\subseteq U_i(E^{\mathrm{sh}})$ with union $G(E^{\mathrm{sh}})$, and integers $c_i$ such that $v(b_{ij}(x))\geq c_i$ for $x\in C_i$ and all $j$. Here $v$ is the valuation of $R^{\mathrm{sh}}$, extended by $v(0)=+\infty$. An open $U\subseteq Y$ of a $T$-scheme is $T$-dense if $U_s$ is dense in $Y_s$ for both $s\in T$. A $T$-rational map is an equivalence class of morphisms on $T$-dense opens, where representatives agree on a $T$-dense open of their common domain. A $T$-birational map is represented by an isomorphism between $T$-dense open subschemes. There is a smooth separated finite-type $T$-scheme $Y$, with nonempty special fibre and an isomorphism $Y_E\simeq G$, with the following property. For every smooth finite-type $T$-scheme $Z$, every generic point $\xi$ of $Z_k$, and $A=\mathcal O_{Z,\xi}$ with fraction field $L$, the ring $A$ is a discrete valuation ring; each left or right translation of $G_L$ by any $g\in G(L)$ extends to an $\operatorname{Spec}A$-birational self-map of $Y_A$, represented by an open immersion on its domain of definition. No group law on $Y$ or mapping property for $Y$ is asserted.

proof.text: Choose a nowhere vanishing left-invariant top form $\omega$ on $G$, and the character $\chi$ describing right translations, by the invariant-volume lemma. Choose a finite weak Néron family with nonempty irreducible special fibres. Let $n_i$ be its differential orders and $n_0=\min_i n_i$. For any other such smooth model $M$, the weak rational property extends the generic identity to $M\dashrightarrow M_i$ for some $i$. Its multiplier is $1$, so order comparison gives $n(M)\geq n_i\geq n_0$. Thus the minimum is attained. The minimal-class lemma supplies finitely many representatives $M_1,\ldots,M_r$. For distinct representatives a rational identity map would, by equal-order comparison, be an open immersion with fibrewise dense image; it would be a birational equivalence, contrary to their choice. The gluing lemma therefore gives opens $V_i$ and a smooth separated finite-type scheme $Y$ by gluing them along $G$. Its special fibre is a nonempty disjoint union of the $(V_i)_k$. All these opens still have order $n_0$.

source.place: 4.3 Proposition 2 and Proposition 4, first two proof paragraphs; 3.5 Theorem 2 and Proposition 3; 4.2 Corollary 3.

proof.text: Fix $Z,\xi,A,L$ as in the statement. The weak-family lemma gives that $A$ is a DVR with uniformizer $\pi$ and base-changes the weak family to $A$. Its converse gives boundedness of $G_L(L^{\mathrm{sh}})$ over $A$. The minimal-class base-change lemma gives that the opens of the $V_i\times_R A$ obtained by retaining one special-fibre component have order $n_0$ and represent all minimal classes over $A$. Smoothness, separatedness and finite type of $Y_A$ follow by the cited base-change statements. Hence each special component of $Y_A$ has order $n_0$.

source.place: 3.5 Corollary 4; 4.3 Lemma 3 and Proposition 4, final sentence.

proof.text: Let $\tau$ be either translation by $g\in G(L)$. By the invariant-volume lemma over $A$, its multiplier on $\omega_L$ is $1$ for a left translation and $\chi_L(g)\in A^\times$ for a right translation. For an open $U\subseteq Y_A$ consisting of the entire generic fibre and a single special component, apply the weak rational property to $\tau:U_L\to G_L$, refining the base-changed weak family into irreducible-special-fibre opens. This gives an $A$-rational map $U\dashrightarrow N$ to a member of that family. Order comparison gives $n_0=n(U)\geq n(N)$; minimality gives the reverse inequality. Thus $N$ is minimal, and its generic identity extends birationally to one of the component opens $P$ of $Y_A$. Compose on the inverse image of the base-dense domain of this identification. The first map is an open immersion by equal-order comparison; its image is fibrewise dense in $N$, so this inverse image is base-dense. We obtain an $A$-rational map $U\dashrightarrow P\subseteq Y_A$ extending $\tau$.

source.place: 4.3 Proposition 4, verification of (iii), together with Lemma 1 and 4.2 Proposition 5.

proof.text: As the special component varies, these maps agree on overlapping domains because their generic restrictions are $\tau$ and the target is separated; use the uniqueness clause of the cited rational-spreading statement, now over the DVR $A$. Their union is therefore an $A$-rational self-map $t$ of $Y_A$ extending $\tau$. Repeat for $\tau^{-1}$. Equal-order comparison on the finite-component models shows that $t$ is an open immersion on its entire domain of definition; the same holds for its inverse-translation extension. Each image contains the entire generic fibre and is dense in every special component. Indeed, step 3 sends each special component $C$ of $Y_A$ to a component $P_C$, and $\tau^{-1}$ sends $P_C$ to some $Q$; composing on the dense inverse image gives an $A$-rational map $C\dashrightarrow Q$ extending the identity of $G_L$. On its domain $W$ this map and the inclusion $W\subseteq Y_A$ agree on the generic fibre, so they are equal by the uniqueness clause of the rational-spreading statement; hence $Q=C$. Thus $C\mapsto P_C$ and the corresponding map for $\tau^{-1}$ are mutually inverse on the finite set of special components, so they are permutations. Intersect the two domains with the inverse images of one another. The resulting opens remain base-dense by this permutation of special components, and the composites are identities by generic uniqueness. Hence $t$ is represented by an isomorphism between $\operatorname{Spec}A$-dense opens. This proves precisely the required birational translation property for both left and right translations.
